current.text: Robinson and Neemias Queta compete for the starting center job in Boston.
The newest expert view is that he will start over Queta. One expert only says he might start.
Expect about 22 to 25 minutes a night and only 55 to 60 games.
Expect him to sit every back-to-back.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Brooklyn for the most in the league.
Boston plays 4, 3 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is one game short of the maximum, and the window has three back-to-backs.
Boston plans to play four shooters around a big in the dunker spot, which is his role.
Expect about 6 points a game, and his FT% could fall to around 30%.
He is a late pick at most. He went around pick 126 to 127 in recent mocks, and one expert would not take him at a Yahoo ADP of 108.
He is worth a stash because he might start or Queta might get hurt. He also works as a category-league streamer, but check Boston's back-to-backs first.

durable.text: He helps FG%, rebounds and blocks and little else. His blocks have dropped off.
He is a very poor free throw shooter. Last season he had the worst FT% in the top 200 (40.8%) and was one of the most harmful FT impact players.
He has no shooting range and makes no threes.
He gives vertical spacing as a pick-and-roll lob threat and a dunker-spot big.
He has a history of ankle problems and missed games. His ankles and foul trouble limit his minutes, and he does not play back-to-backs.

note: The sites split on him. Yahoo ranks him 173rd at 0 USD and ESPN ranks him 116th at 2 USD, and recent mocks took him around pick 126. With 144 players drafted, that puts him on the edge between a 1 USD final pick and waivers. He only makes sense in punt FT% builds that want FG% (70% projected), rebounds and blocks from a center. Early in the season, check whether he starts over Queta, whether he plays more than about 22 minutes, and whether he sits all of Boston's 16 back-to-backs. Three of those back-to-backs fall in our playoff weeks.
